content: 1. The glycoprotein MDR1 (P-glycoprotein) efflux transporter plays a role in drug interactions. Red yeast rice can increase the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting this transporter. Use caution and monitor for potential increased toxicity. 2. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. 4. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 5. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 6. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. 7. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 8. Co-administration of maraviroc with sacubitril/valsartan can lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 9. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates, and consider dosage reduction if necessary. 10. Co-administration of maraviroc with selegiline can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 11. Maraviroc increases the levels of sertraline by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential increased toxicity. 12. Co-administration of maraviroc with sildenafil can lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 13. Co-administration of maraviroc with silodosin can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 14. Sirolimus increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 15. Somatropin decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 16. Co-administration of maraviroc with spironolactone can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 17. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 18. Stiripentol affects maraviroc levels by inhibiting and inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Stiripentol also inhibits P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, potentially increasing maraviroc levels. Consider reducing the dose of P-gp substrates if adverse reactions occur. 19. Tacrolimus increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 20. Co-administration of maraviroc with tadalafil can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 21. Maraviroc decreases the effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, reducing the formation of tamoxifen’s active metabolite, endoxifen. Use caution and monitor. 22. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by weakly inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 24. Co-administration of maraviroc with telmisartan can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 25. Co-administration of maraviroc with terazosin can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 26. Co-administration of maraviroc with thiothixene can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 27. Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of timolol by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Co-administration of maraviroc with tizanidine can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 29. Tocilizumab decreases the levels of maraviroc by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 30. Tolvaptan increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 31. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 34. Use caution and monitor. 36. Co-administration of maraviroc with treprostinil can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 37. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 38. Co-administration of maraviroc with trimipramine can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 39. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 40. Ublituximab decreases the effects of maraviroc due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 41. Co-administration of maraviroc with valsartan can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 42. Co-administration of maraviroc with vardenafil can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 43. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 44. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 45. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 46. Co-administration of maraviroc with ziprasidone can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Use caution and monitor for an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 47. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 48. Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of amphetamine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 49. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 50. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can lower the exposure of CYP3A4 substrates. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if co-administration is necessary.
